edits.old: Then t is dominated (by v) if (and only if) occ(v) > occ(v') for any other number v'. For example, arrays [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 2], [11, 11] and [3, 2, 3, 2, 3] are dominated (by 2, 11 and 3 respectevitely) but arrays [3], [1, 2] and [3, 3, 2, 2, 1] are not.
edits.new: Then t is dominated by v if and only if occ(v) ≥ 3 and occ(v) > occ(v') for every other number v'. For example, [3,2,3,2,3] is dominated by 3. Arrays [1,2,3,4,5,2], [11,11], [3], [1,2] and [3,3,2,2,1] are not dominated under this rule.
